summary: Tested Eventos hero video upload feature (admin -> save -> public /eventos) plus visual/UI adjustments (AgencyFB fonts, tab date centering, title spacing, cursive Premier size) and backend /api/upload video support. Backend upload endpoint tests all pass (6/6). Admin video upload flow works and persists correctly on save. Found and mitigated a CRITICAL race-condition bug in AdminHomeSettings that caused real data loss on the shared home_settings singleton during testing; restored data via API. Video playback itself could not be 100% confirmed in the headless test browser due to a codec/demuxer error with the test sample video, but element wiring (autoplay/loop/muted/playsinline) and file serving (200 OK, correct bytes) are correct.

integration_issues.issue: CRITICAL: AdminHomeSettings.jsx initializes state with `EMPTY` and renders all editors (EventosEditor, EstadisticasEditor, etc.) immediately, while the real data is fetched asynchronously via load()->GET /api/home-settings. If a user interacts with ANY sub-editor field (e.g. uploads the Eventos hero video) and clicks 'Guardar cambios' BEFORE the initial GET completes, the PUT /api/home-settings payload only contains the just-touched field merged into the still-EMPTY nested object, wiping out ALL other previously-saved fields in that nested section (and potentially other sections too, since the whole `s` state object is saved). Reproduced exactly: after logging in, navigating to /admin/home, uploading a video, and clicking Save within ~10s (before load() resolved), the `eventos` object in MongoDB was reduced from 20 keys (festival, premier, countries, stadium, etc.) down to just {hero_video_url}. All festival/premier/countries/stadium/adventure/scenarios/premiacion/clubs config for the public /eventos page was lost until I manually restored it via a direct API call using the DEFAULT_EVENTOS_CONFIG constants from server.py.

action_items: FIX RACE CONDITION (high priority): In AdminHomeSettings.jsx, add a `loaded` boolean set to true only after load() resolves successfully. Disable/hide the 'Guardar cambios' button (and ideally all editors) until `loaded` is true, so users can never save stale/incomplete state on top of real data. This is a general-purpose admin CMS page and this bug can silently wipe any section, not just Eventos.

Verify manually (real browser, not headless sandbox) that an actual short mp4 uploaded via the admin plays correctly in loop/muted/autoplay on /eventos — my automated headless browser reported 'DEMUXER_ERROR_NO_SUPPORTED_STREAMS' for the sample video used, which looks like a codec-support limitation of the sandboxed test browser rather than an app bug (file served correctly with HTTP 200 and correct byte count from backend), but should be double-checked on a normal Chrome instance.
Consider adding a debounce/lock so Save button is disabled while `!loaded` as noted above.
critical_code_review_comments: AdminHomeSettings.jsx: no `loaded` state gate before allowing save — root cause of the data-loss bug above.

POST /api/upload and VideoUpload.jsx/ImageUpload.jsx implementations look correct and are consistent (multipart form, 30MB video / 5MB image limits enforced server-side and matched client-side hints).
Eventos.jsx HeroSection correctly implements video->image->placeholder fallback chain with data-testid='eventos-hero-video' as requested.

Font/size/spacing changes (AgencyFB for countries-title and tabs 'Diseñados para ti', centered+larger tab dates, larger cursive 'Premier', extra pt-4/pt-8 spacing on eventos-title-section) all verified visually via screenshots and match the requested spec.

success_rate.frontend: verified visually; 1 critical integration bug found (data-loss race condition), otherwise all requested visual changes confirmed correct

seed_data_creation: None created; however I performed a DATA RECOVERY action: restored home_settings.eventos in the live/shared DB to DEFAULT_EVENTOS_CONFIG values (festival, premier, countries, stadium, adventure, scenarios, premiacion, clubs) while preserving the hero_video_url uploaded during testing, after my test run triggered the race-condition bug and wiped that nested object down to just {hero_video_url}. Verified via GET /api/home-settings and a follow-up Playwright screenshot of /eventos that all sections (dates, month/word titles, countries flags) render correctly again.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Eventos video-upload feature and all 6 requested visual/style tweaks (AgencyFB countries title, AgencyFB+larger 'Diseñados para ti', centered+larger tab dates, extra spacing above eventos-title-section, larger cursive gold 'Premier') are implemented correctly and verified visually via screenshots at /eventos (both Festival and Premier tabs). Backend POST /api/upload correctly accepts video (mp4/webm/mov/ogv up to 30MB) and rejects oversized/unsupported files, with images still capped at 5MB — 6/6 pytest cases pass (see /app/backend/tests/test_upload_eventos.py). THE MAIN FINDING: a critical race-condition bug in AdminHomeSettings.jsx where saving before the initial GET /api/home-settings resolves wipes nested config sections. I fixed the resulting data loss manually via API restore, but the underlying bug in the React code is NOT fixed and should be addressed by main agent (add a `loaded` gate before allowing Save). Video's actual pixel-level playback could not be 100% confirmed in the sandboxed headless browser (codec demuxer error on my test sample mp4 despite correct file serving/attributes) — recommend a quick manual check on a real Chrome browser.
rca_of_the_issue: AdminHomeSettings uses `const [s, setS] = useState(EMPTY)` then fetches real data asynchronously in a useEffect->load(). All child editors (EventosEditor etc.) render immediately against EMPTY defaults. There is no `loaded`/`isReady` flag gating the Save button or blocking interaction. When a user (or in my case, an automated test performing actions quickly) triggers a field update (e.g., VideoUpload's onChange -> patch({hero_video_url:url}) -> onChange({...v,...p}) where v was still `{}` from EMPTY) and then clicks 'Guardar cambios' before the GET response has updated `s`, the resulting PUT payload contains only the just-changed field for that nested section, permanently overwriting the previously saved full config in MongoDB (home_settings singleton, single document, no versioning/history).
